title: Cold-to-Warm Ramp & Eviction Interplay benchmark for KV prefix cache
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Purpose: quantify how cold-to-warm traffic ramps interact with eviction policy and memory budget to affect tokens/sec, p95 latency, and cache hit-rate for the KV prefix cache. The goal is to produce an automated benchmark/harness that covers steady-state and transient ramp scenarios representative of real Redwood workloads (bursty PLG onboarding, background workers, multi-tenant spikes). This ticket covers harness design, a hardware sweep across instance shapes, baseline capture, and a regression detector that raises alerts when p95 or tokens/sec degrade beyond defined thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Deliver harness that can run deterministic cold-to-warm ramp scenarios and produce token/sec and p95 latency time series
Baseline data collected for 4 instance classes (g4dn.4xlarge equivalent, p3.2x, p4d.smallx, and a high-memory 512GB variant) and for 3 eviction policies (LRU, LFU, Segmented-LRU)

Regression detector implemented: compares new run to baseline using a sliding-window p95 comparison and raises GitHub issue if p95 increases by >20% or tokens/sec drops by >15% sustained for 5 minutes
Bench results pushed to /benchmarks/kv/warmup-eviction-2026Q1 with metadata JSON and Grafana dashboard link
Run time < 90 minutes for a full sweep with automated teardown and artifact upload
test_plan: Synthetic traffic generator with adjustable hotspot skewness (Zipf alpha 0.7/1.2/1.8), sequence length distribution (32/128/512), and prefix lengths sampled from production prefix histogram
Cold start: prefill cache with 0% hotset, ramp traffic from 0 to target QPS over 60s, hold at steady-state for 10 minutes, then inject eviction pressure by increasing unique keys per second
Warm start: pre-warm cache to 80% hit rate, then vary memory budget downward in 10% steps to simulate memory contention
Measure tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, hit-rate over sliding 30s windows, GC/CPU utilization, and per-shard tail latency
Repeat each scenario 3 times and compute median/95th confidence interval
harness_config: batch_size: auto (runtime chooses by target latency SLO); override options: 1/8/32
concurrency_profiles: steady, bursty (90th percentile bursts: 5x baseline), sustained high-throughput
observed_results: Preliminary run (p4d.smallx equiv, SegmentedLRU, 75% mem): tokens/sec=245k, p95=48ms, hit-rate=84% (median of 3 repeats)
Cold-to-warm ramp exposes a 2x p95 spike during first 45s as KV misses cause KV-fetch pipelines to saturate; impact reduced by increasing kv_shards from 8->32
LRU at 50% mem budget showed oscillatory hit-rate behavior under bursty skew (Zipf alpha=1.8) leading to sustained p95 variance (stdev p95 across windows +28%)
LFU maintained steadier hit-rate under high skew but increased average eviction compute leading to higher CPU; tokens/sec plateau lower by ~9% compared to SegmentedLRU in steady state
On the high-memory 512GB variant, hit-rate improvements are marginal beyond 75% budget for realistic hotset sizes; diminishing returns observed for memory>400GB
Regression detector false positives seen when host-level GC runs coincided with ramp windows; added host-metrics filter to ignore p95 spikes aligned with full-GC events
